newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat futures quiet, testing lows again.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat futures quiet, testing lows again.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures continued to trade quietly on Friday, ending a dull week.
November 1997 fell by 50 cents to A$145.00 a tonne in four trades. January 1997 edged up by 50 cents on the settlement price to A$151.50.
First notice for deliveries on the Chicago December contract later on Friday had taken the market down to the bottom end of the trading range, Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd said.
Continued downside pressure meant a close below US$3.80 a bushel in Chicago would test previous lows, he said.
"It's looking as if its just running a little bit out of steam," Hillary said.
Next week would test support levels in Australia after the return to work in the U.S. markets, he said.
The Australian market would not move until the U.S. showed direction first, he added.
If SFE wheat traded beneath A$148.00, downside pressure would intensify.
Upside trades above A$160.00 would be interesting for a possible rally, but were not expected, he said.
